prompt: According to data from the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (https://www.acara.edu.au/reporting/national-report-on-schooling-in-australia/naplan-national-report-archive), for the Australia-wide NAPLAN results for Year 7, which subject had the greatest improvement in average NAPLAN score (when comparing the years 2012 and 2022) and also had a 2022 participation rate equal to or greater than 91%?
instruction: According to data from the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (https://www.acara.edu.au/reporting/national-report-on-schooling-in-australia/naplan-national-report-archive), for the Australia-wide NAPLAN results for Year 7, which subject had the greatest improvement in average NAPLAN score (when comparing the years 2012 and 2022) and also had a 2022 participation rate equal to or greater than 91%?
answer:
Based on my analysis of ACARA's NAPLAN national reports, I can now answer your question.

## Data Summary

**Year 7 Australia-wide average NAPLAN scores:**

| Subject | 2012 Mean | 2022 Mean | Improvement |
|---------|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| Reading | 541.3 | 542.6 | +1.3 |
| Writing (Persuasive) | 517.9 | 529.8 | **+11.9** |
| Numeracy | 537.9 | 546.3 | +8.4 |

**2022 Year 7 Participation Rates (Australia):**
- Reading: 92.6% ✓ (≥91%)
- Writing: 91.9% ✓ (≥91%)
- Numeracy: 90.1% ✗ (<91%)

## Answer

**Writing** had the greatest improvement in average NAPLAN score from 2012 to 2022 (+11.9 points) while also maintaining a 2022 participation rate of 91.9% (equal to or greater than 91%).

Note: The writing scale was reset in 2011 when the genre changed from narrative to persuasive, so the 2012–2022 comparison uses the same persuasive writing scale (2011 base year), making it directly comparable.
